newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Slammed by one storm, Philippines braces for next.
newsitem.headline: Slammed by one storm, Philippines braces for next.

text.p: The Philippines, barely recovered from a storm that killed at least 16 people, braced on Sunday for a more powerful typhoon with winds gusting up to 210 kph (130 mph).

President Fidel Ramos placed 14 provincial and eight cities under a state calamity in the wake of storm Ernie which pounded the country's central and southern regions in the past week, triggering floods and mudslides that damaged more than 2,000 houses.
A day after Ernie left the country, typhoon Dale on Sunday moved closer to the northern Philippines with centre winds of 175 kph (108 mph) and gusts of 210 kph (130 mph), the weather bureau said.
It said Dale, the 17th storm to threaten this typhoon-prone country this year, was located 1,090 km (675 miles) east-southeast of Cagayan province headed towards northern Batanes island.
A calamity declaration is an administrative device that allows the release of emergency funds for rebuilding damaged areas.
Ernie damaged property and agricultural crops worth 24.5 million pesos ($950,000), the civil defence office said.
